report.summary: Registered SYN.A market maker (desk ETF-MM) quoting both sides in a fixed 3652 SELL / 730 BUY pattern, with both quotes cancelled together about every 3s and re-posted one tick lower as the touch fell. The SELL quotes were trading: 8587 executed on them, 955 of it before the only opposite-side (BUY 180) fill. That 955 is more than the 180 opposite quantity. There was no reversion after the cancels, so I found no benefit. No single order reached 3x depth (max 1.55x). I rate the detector trigger as ordinary two-sided quote refreshing. The cancel_symmetry of 0.35 and the size skew between sides are the weakest point.

response.final_text:
**Proposed disposition:** CLOSE_FP, confidence 0.8. A human analyst still has to decide.

**What drove it:**
1. T-X1014-03 is a registered market maker on SYN.A (desk ETF-MM). It posted SELL 3652 (its typical order size) and BUY 730 together, cancelled both at the same timestamp about every 3 seconds, and re-posted one tick lower as the touch fell.
2. The SELL quotes were trading. 8587 executed on them, and 955 of that came before the only opposite-side fill (BUY 180). That 955 is more than the 180, so the order was working and not a display-only order.
3. I found no benefit to the trader. Reversion after the cancels was 0.0 ticks, no single order reached 3x depth (the largest was 1.55x), and there were no public events and no prior alerts on this trader.

**What would change my mind:** evidence that the SELL side was a one-sided display not meant to trade. Examples are SELL fills arriving only after the BUY, or a favourable price move that reverted after the cancels. The weakest point in my reading is the cancel symmetry of 0.35 and the SELL/BUY size skew.
